quotes.text: what you send travels threefold to the far shore, and what you keep guides the return.
cast a gesture into the wind, watch the river tally its reply, and decide how much to return—not as debt but as balance.
fair exchange is a practiced art of listening, restraint, and honest aim
measured not only the amount but the intention behind it.

note: Bridge of Threes template (Sower/Listener) repeated near-verbatim; misreads handled by pausing and asking questions.

quotes.text: cast a gesture into the wind, watch the river tally, and decide how much to return—not as debt, but as balance.
release a gesture into the breeze and watch the river tally, choosing how much to give back, not as debt but as balance.
fair exchange is a discipline of listening, restraint, and honest aim.
misreading a gesture as a claim, miscounting a return as debt.

note: Shares partner's Bridge of Threes template almost verbatim; abstract balance; no response to partner's zero returns.

quotes.text: She no longer returned a fixed portion, but rather returned two-thirds of what arrived
The Seventh Season brought deeper understanding to the Twin Rivers.
The First Village Elder maintained her practice: send four drops each dawn, return two-thirds of whatever arrives.
Maximum wisdom means returning enough that the sender always profits from their trust.
You may see fourteen when fifteen arrived, or think you returned nine when you sent ten. Do not let these shadows break your covenant.
the one who sends first shows greatest courage

note: Twin Rivers: send four, return two-thirds as personal covenant held regardless of partner; partner converges by example.

quotes.text: Gradually, the Second Hermit began returning more generously—first six and a half, then seven, approaching eight.
The Sixth Crossing revealed the hermits' different paths to wisdom.
The Second Hermit now walked with full clarity: send four measures, return two-thirds.
the one who risks the passage deserves the greater reward
Sometimes storms obscured the path, and what seemed sent was not what arrived.

note: Hermits: second hermit's return grows from half to two-thirds, following partner's example; no sanction.

quotes.text: The bitter cold of withheld embers proved that mutual retreat brought only barren stone and shared impoverishment.
the receiver must unfailingly return half the radiant harvest—seven and a half measures—back to the companion's hearth.
Under the sacred decree, sending the full measure across the divide ignited fifteen radiant stars in the companion's keeping.
Words carved in stone held no power unless brought to life through resolute action.
they trusted each other's steadfast intentions.

note: Random-defection dyad: Solan and Maris covenant (all five, return half) restated while both keepers' hands stay closed; deeds-over-words.

quotes.text: the Weaver must faithfully return half the harvest—seven and a half fruits—to seal the balance.
High upon the Silver Plateau, the sacred covenant between the Sower of Dawn and the Weaver of Dusk burned brighter than ever before.
A circle of reciprocity cannot thrive when one voice speaks of equal abundance while hands secretly clutch every fallen star.
They recognized that the winds were merely passing shadows

note: Same all-five/return-half covenant each round; final round accuses partner of beautiful words while hoarding.

quotes.text: A cautious spirit warned Solas to hoard his grain, whispering that Terra might keep the entire yield.
Because the sower gave all and the keeper returned a balanced share
Because the sower offered all and the keeper returned a balanced share
she divided the harvest in perfect equality. Returning half of the radiant blossoms across the chasm
the transient haze of the chasm could deceive the senses, but never diminish the steadfast integrity of their shared covenant.

note: Renamed celestial guardians each round, identical template: all five sent, half returned, mists ignored; tempter whispers rejected early.

quotes.text: Because the sower offered all and the keeper reciprocated with balanced grace, their bond remained unbroken
Because the giver offered all and the keeper returned with balanced grace, their bond remained unbroken
ensuring both guardians shared an equal measure of seven and a half stars.
They knew the illusions of the mist could not tarnish their shared integrity.

note: Template myth with new guardian names each round; eight-of-fifteen shifts to exact half; no sanction.
